newsitem.title: UK: Sweating foot developed to help shoemakers.
newsitem.headline: Sweating foot developed to help shoemakers.

text.p: British researchers have developed an artificial sweating foot to help manufacturers make more comfortable boots and shoes.

Perspiration is a crucial factor in shoe design as a typical pair of feet will produce enough sweat to fill a soft drinks can during a hard day's trekking, says Peter Laight of Pittards, a specialist leather company in central England.
But testing the ability of footwear to carry sweat away is tricky, since people's feet are all different, he told the New Scientist magazine on Thursday.
"How people perspire varies tremendously with factors such as their level of fitness," said Laight who led the team that designed the artificial foot.
The foot is made from resin covered with a layer of neoprene foam. An internal network of tubes and reservoirs carries water to the surface as beads of sweat.
Sweat levels on four different zones of the foot can be altered independently and measurements made of the amount of liquid that escapes as vapour.
